name: ALPHA
summary: The international ALPHA collaboration proposes artificial plasma materials to detect higher-mass QCD axions.
detection_principle: A metamaterial of parallel wires provides a tunable effective plasma frequency, enhancing observable electromagnetic excitations on axion resonance.

status.label: Construction and subsystem commissioning
status.evidence: The collaboration's DPF2026 report describes commissioning and then projected first science operation in early 2028; this is a planned, not achieved, date.

timeline.event: ALPHA Consortium established (as documented on the official project page).
First collaboration meeting held at Yale Wright Lab.
Phase I design and sensitivity projections published.

collaboration.name: ALPHA Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

key_parameters.name: Phase I design scan
key_parameters.value: 10–20 GHz, approximately 40–80 μeV; design sensitivity approaches KSVZ.

results.summary: The initial design and R&D / commissioning progress are public; these sources report no completed cosmic-axion-search limit.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
